name: Dionysus
text: Dionysus was an ancient Greek deity linked to wine and to fertility rites. His cult favoured ecstatic celebration. The Greeks adapted the figure from an earlier Lydian god. The Romans called the same figure Bacchus. They also called him Liber. Some twentieth-century scholars drew a parallel with the Irish hero Lug Lámfhota. The parallel rested on shared features of cult and seasonal festival. Michael Tierney argued the case in a 1963 article in Éigse. The article is titled Lughnasa and Dionysus. The comparison still draws scholarly attention today.

okr.objective: Dionysus as the Greek deity linked to wine and to possible Irish parallels in Lug Lámfhota.
